We have applied template 1914393 and got a tuple of two SMILES? The result is "(('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'),)". That seems to be a tuple containing a pair of SMILES: first product? Actually apply_template returns list of precursor SMILES. It returned a tuple of one pair: ('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'). So the retrosynthetic step splits target into two fragments: fragment A: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 (looks like target without the side chain containing CCl? Actually original target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. After applying template, we get fragment A: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 (the core heterocycle with NH not N? and fragment B: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 (a fluorinated azetidine? Actually it's a morpholine? It's a fluorinated piperidine? Anyway). So we need to continue retrosynthesis using templates 1914394 then 1914395 in order.

Now we need to apply template 1914394 to one of the fragments? Probably to fragment B (the side chain) to break the CCl? Template 1914394 seems to involve a Cl-CH2-Cl leaving group? The retro smarts: [#7:3]-[C:4]-[c:5]1...>>Cl-[CH2]-[Cl] plus aromatic. So it likely disconnects a chloromethyl group attached to aromatic. Our fragment B has CCl attached to aromatic: Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2. So applying template 1914394 to fragment B should give precursors: aromatic with CH2Cl? Actually the template seems to break a C-Cl bond and generate Cl-CH2-Cl? Wait the forward reaction: aromatic with CH2Cl attached? The retro template: product is aromatic with CH2Cl? Let's just apply to fragment B.
